neighbours.label: the preposition that introduces what something is exchanged for (trade X for Y, paid in dollars)
fire: At the market he traded his old watch for a sack of rice.
In the camp the prisoners swapped cigarettes for extra bread.
Would you really give up your weekend for a small bonus?
Along the desert route merchants exchanged salt for gold.
Last week she sold her bicycle for forty dollars.
The farmer bartered three goats for a new plough.
Most of these oil contracts are paid for in dollars.
The kids offered their candy for a turn on the swing.
quiet: At the market he bought rice for his whole family.
In the camp the prisoners waited for extra bread.
Would you really work this weekend for your team?
Along the desert route merchants travelled for weeks.
Last week she rode her bicycle for forty minutes.
The farmer kept three goats for many years.
Most of these oil contracts are signed in London.
The kids waited patiently for a turn on the swing.

notes: Card: peaks on ' for' after exchanged/offering/give up, ' in' after 'paid for', ' of' debt in buying. Near misses keep the topic and use 'for' / 'in' in a non-exchange sense.
